# Quality: Kition

This file is the entry point for testing Kition. It applies to people and to AI agents. The
"Quality rules (read first)" section at the top of `AGENTS.md` is the short version; this file
is the reference.

Tests are the spec. The feature catalogue (`features.yaml`) and each case's `intent` say how
this repository must behave. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless the owner
approves changing it.

## Five directions

Every feature and every case belongs to one or more of these directions.

| Direction | What is tested | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `function` | Every command (menu item, shortcut, tool) works, takes the right parameters, and can be undone; interactions (click, drag, type, select) | The command's design and the expected state after the interaction |
| `conversion` | Open and save without loss (round trip); conversion between formats | Round trip: the document model (KDM) before and after; across formats: the reference tool's output |
| `ai` | The six agent abilities: observe, operate, execute, validate, recover, share | The expected result of each tool call; the task's completion criteria |
| `collab` | People and agents editing at once converge; draft merges; reconnects; offline sync | Every replica ends equal; merges follow the rules |
| `fidelity` | Rendering, layout, formula results, charts, fonts, compared with the target application | The reference tool's output: cached formula values saved by Excel, PDFs and PNGs exported by Word, PowerPoint, WPS or Photoshop |

`features.yaml` also uses `compat`, `performance`, `robustness`, `data-safety`, `platform` and
`security` for the tests outside these five.

## Four layers

| `layer` | Runs | Budget | Failing means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | Not executed by the case runner: the case points at an existing test (`cargo-test` or `exec` step) that `pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s lint` already runs. The runner only checks the test exists, so the catalogue links to it | (inside `pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s lint`) | The commit is refused by `pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s lint` |
| `golden` | Every commit, every PR, before an agent ends a task (`cargo xtask golden --affected`; all before merge) | The whole kit ≤ `golden_budget_s` (600) on the owner's machine | Not done; cannot merge |
| `corpus` | Weekly, on the owner's machine at night | Hours | Weekly report; important failures become issues and then regression cases |
| `ai` | Only when the owner starts it (`cargo xtask ai`, F-QA-16): never from a hook, golden, the pre-finish check, a schedule, CI, or by an agent on its own | Tokens are recorded, not capped | Success rate per kit and model in the run's report; the matrix reads the latest owner run |

## How to run

```sh
pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s lint
```

Run it before you finish any task; the task is not done until it exits 0. Report the real exit
code, not the exit code of a wrapper shell. When the golden case runner arrives, this section
names `cargo xtask golden --affected` (the golden cases of the features you touched) as well.

Claude Code runs this command through the Stop hook in `.claude/settings.json`
(`.claude/hooks/quality-gate.sh`). For an emergency bypass in one session only, start it with
`KITION_SKIP_QUALITY_HOOK=1`; say so in the task's findings.

### Agents without hooks (Codex and others)

Codex has no blocking Stop hook. Before you report a task as done:

1. Run the command above and wait for it to finish.
2. Report the command and its real exit code in your final message. A non-zero exit code means
   the task is not done.
3. Run `node <kition-sdk>/tools/check-expected.mjs origin/main..HEAD` from the repository root
   (`<kition-sdk>` is your kition-sdk checkout). If it lists anything, name each entry in your
   final message so the owner can review it.

## Where things are

```text
features.yaml          the feature catalogue (the only source; edit this)
FEATURES.md            generated from features.yaml; never edit by hand
QUALITY.md             this file
cases/
  <feature-id>/
    <case-slug>/
      case.yaml        the case (required)
      input/           input files (small, clean licence)
      expected/        expected results (protected)
  regressions/
    issue-<n>/         a case from an issue in this repository
    issue-<repo>-<n>/  a case from an issue in another repository
conformance/           the agent conformance fixtures (cases refer to them, never copy them)
corpus/                the corpus (gitignored; fetched at pinned commits)
kit-waivers.yaml       owner-approved, dated exceptions to requirement rows
```

Outputs of a run go to `target/golden/<case-id>/`, never into `cases/`; a case calls that
directory `out/`.

- **Weekly report**: the nightly kit matrix and the Monday summary (corpus results, AI task
  success, rows that turned red or green, waivers) are kept in the KitionAI planning repository
  (kition-plan). Agents read it on Mondays and pick the failing P0 features first.
- **Requirements**: the rows every kit must meet are in `kit-requirements.yaml` in kition-plan.
  A feature names its rows in `requirements`.
- **Waivers**: `kit-waivers.yaml` at the repository root. A waiver defers a row until a date;
  it never relaxes the row and never permits a compatibility layer. Only the owner approves
  one; agents may propose one with `approved_on: null`.

## How to add a case

1. Find or add the feature in `features.yaml`.
2. Create `cases/<feature-id>/<case-slug>/case.yaml` with an `intent` first, then `input/`
   and `expected/`. Expected results come from the reference the case names, never from the
   code under test (except blessed `self` references).
3. For a bug, create `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/` and show it failing before the fix.
4. Run the command above, then put the case id in the commit message (`Cases: <id>, …`).

### Names

| Name | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Feature id | `<kit>.<area>[.<name>…]`, 2–4 dot-separated segments; each segment lowercase ASCII letters and digits, words joined by `-`; the first segment is the kit's canonical name | `doc.review.comments`, `sheet.formula.xlookup`, `board.collab.same-drag` |
| Case slug | lowercase ASCII, digits and `-`, at most 40 characters, unique within its feature | `basic`, `cjk-grid`, `wps-cover` |
| Case id | `<feature-id>/<case-slug>`; for bugs `regressions/issue-<n>` or `regressions/issue-<repo>-<n>` | `doc.review.comments/thread-roundtrip`, `regressions/issue-kition-1234` |
| Reference file in `expected/` | `<stem>.<WHAT>.<TOOL>.<ext>`: `<WHAT>` is a conversion (`WORDTOPDF`, `PPTXTOPDF`, …) or an extract (`VALUES`, `COMPOSITE`, `SCORECARD`); `<TOOL>` an upper-case tool token | `comments.WORDTOPDF.WPS.pdf`, `xlookup.VALUES.EXCEL.json`, `curves.COMPOSITE.PHOTOSHOP.png` |
| Self reference (made by Kition, guards against regressions only) | `<stem>.<WHAT>.KITION.<ext>` | `page1.RENDER.KITION.png` |

Tool tokens: `WPS`, `WORD`, `EXCEL`, `POWERPOINT`, `ACROBAT`, `PHOTOSHOP`, `M365WEB`, `POPPLER`, `GHOSTSCRIPT`, `PDFJS`, `PSDTOOLS`, `UPSTREAM` (the kit's upstream application, credited in the kit repository's `NOTICE`), `KITION`.

### `case.yaml`

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | int, `1` | yes | Version of this format. A new version rewrites every case in the same commit; no reader for old versions (no compatibility layers) |
| `id` | string | yes | Case id (see Names). Must equal the case's path under `cases/` |
| `feature` | string | yes | Feature id; must exist in `features.yaml`. A regression case names the feature it protects |
| `intent` | string | yes | One or two sentences: what this case guarantees and why it matters. The most important line; the reviewer and the AI read it before touching the behaviour |
| `layer` | enum `unit` \| `golden` \| `corpus` \| `ai` | yes | When it runs (see Four layers). Regression cases are `golden` unless the owner moves them |
| `direction` | enum, see `features.yaml` | no | Defaults to the feature's first direction; set it when this case tests another one |
| `source` | map | yes | Where the case comes from: `kind` (enum `synthetic` \| `golden-sample` \| `corpus` \| `issue` \| `probe` \| `user-file`), `from` (string: sample path, corpus file, issue `<owner>/<repo>#<n>`, report path), `licence` (SPDX id or `owned`), `note` (string, optional). A `user-file` needs the owner's consent recorded in `note`; files that cannot be published are rebuilt as `synthetic` instead |
| `input` | list<string> | yes (may be empty) | Input files. Paths relative to the case directory (`input/…`); `repo:<path>` for a file elsewhere in the repository (for example `repo:conformance/basic.docx`); `corpus:<set>/<glob>` only in `corpus` cases |
| `steps` | list<step> | yes | What to do, in order (see Steps). Each step is a map with one key |
| `expected` | list<expectation> | yes | What must hold afterwards (see Expectations). At least one entry |
| `reference` | list<map> | when any expectation compares with a reference | Who made each reference result: `id` (string), `tool` (tool token), `version` (string, exact), `platform` (string), `made` (date string), `how` (string: menu path or command line and settings), `kind` (enum `external` \| `self`). `external` = the target application or an independent reader is the truth; `self` = a blessed Kition output that only guards against regressions |
| `tolerance` | map | no | Defaults per compare kind for this case (see Tolerance); an expectation may override its own |
| `tags` | list<string> | no | Free labels for selection: `cjk`, `rtl`, `large`, `browser`, `slow`, `security`, `platform-macos` … |
| `since` | string, `YYYY-MM-DD` (quoted) | yes | Date the case was added (or the expected result last approved) |
| `requires` | list<string> | no | External tools the runner needs (`ooxml-validator`, `poppler`, `qpdf`, `verapdf`, `chromium`, `webkit`). In a `golden` case a missing tool is a failure, never a skip |
| `timeout_s` | int | no | Default 20; hard cap 60 for `golden` |

### Steps

Steps use the vocabulary of the kit's agent tools, so a case runs in-process and through the
headless executable alike.

| Step | Value | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | path, or `{ path, password }` | the open document |
| `create` | `{ kind, from? }` | a new document |
| `run` | `{ command, params }`: one engine command | `out:<as>` result when `as` is given |
| `batch` | `{ ops, as? }`: KDM batch (kdm kits) | result |
| `query` | `{ select, as }`: read values or objects (for example a cell range) | named JSON |
| `snapshot` | `{ as }`: the canonical KDM state (A26) | named JSON |
| `recalc` | `{}`: recalculate everything (kits with formulas; the same as running the kit's calculate-now command) | — |
| `check` | `{ as }` | named diagnostics list |
| `inspect` | `{ preview?, layout?, target?, scale?, as }` | named JSON and, with `preview`, a PNG |
| `render` | `{ target, scale?, as }`: what `view.screenshot` returns, by the kit's own engine | named PNG |
| `save` | `out/<file>` | a file in the run's output directory |
| `export` | `{ to: out/<file>, format?, options? }` | a file |
| `reopen` | `out/<file>`: close and open the saved file | the reopened document |
| `cargo-test` | `{ package, test?, filter?, features?, env? }`: run an existing test; `env` values starting with `expected/`, `out/` or `corpus/` are resolved to real paths | exit status and, through `env`, report files |
| `exec` | `{ cmd: [..], env? }`: run a repository tool (for example `khp-agent-conformance`) | exit status, stdout |
| `flow` | `{ spec, scenario, browsers }`: a scenario of the kit's `web/tests/flow.mjs` | exit status, screenshots |
| `task` | `{ prompt, files, models, max_turns }`: `ai` layer only | the agent's output files and a transcript with token counts |

Names given with `as` are referred to in `expected` as `out:<name>`; saved files as `out/<file>`.

### Expectations

Each entry: `actual` (an `out:` name or `out/` file), `compare` (kind below), then either `file` (an `expected/` file), `against` (another `out:` name, for before/after comparisons), or `value` (inline, for small values), plus optional `reference` (a `reference[].id`) and `tolerance`.

| `compare` | Compares | Typical source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `kdm-json` | canonical KDM JSON, after removing `ignore` paths | before/after the round trip (`against`); a blessed snapshot |
| `png` | pixels, with a pixel tolerance | target application's export; Photoshop's merged composite stored in the PSD; a blessed render |
| `pdf-structure` | page count, page sizes, per-page text, embedded fonts | the target application's PDF export |
| `values` | a map of keys to numbers, strings, booleans or error codes | the cached results Excel stores in the file |
| `text` | bytes or lines | the input itself (note's Markdown round trip) |
| `diagnostics` | codes and targets of `check` | the check catalogue (`agent/checks.json`, A38) |
| `package` | the saved package against a validator | `ooxml-structure` (the checks of the doc and sheet probes), `ooxml-schema`, `qpdf`, `verapdf`, `psd-strict` |
| `scorecard` | an existing fidelity scorecard must not drop below a baseline | the accepted baseline in `expected/` |
| `exit` | exit status `0` | the step itself (for `cargo-test`, `exec`, `flow`) |

### Tolerance

| Compare | Fields (all optional; every given field must hold) | Presets |
|---|---|---|
| `png` | `max_abs` (0–255, largest channel difference), `p99` (0–255), `mean_abs` (number), `min_psnr` (dB), `channel_threshold` (0–255) with `max_diff_ratio` (0–1, share of pixels whose largest channel difference exceeds the threshold), `dpi` (raster PDFs before comparing), `region` (`[x, y, w, h]`) | `exact` = `max_abs: 0`; `render` = `min_psnr: 45, max_abs: 12, p99: 2` (kition-film `testkit` `Tolerance::RENDER`); `oracle` = `max_abs: 2` (kition-photo: renders like Photoshop at ≤ 2/255); `cross-tool` = `channel_threshold: 48, max_diff_ratio: 0.01` (kition-pdf probe against poppler) |
| `values` | `rel` (default `1e-9`), `abs` (default `0`), `skip_volatile` (default `true`: `NOW`, `TODAY`, `RAND*`, `INFO`, `CELL`) | — |
| `kdm-json` | `ignore` (list of JSON-pointer globs), `float_abs` (default `0`; sizes may use `0.01`, as `fidelity.rs` does for pixels and points) | — |
| `pdf-structure` | `page_count` (allowed difference, default `0`), `page_size_pt` (default `0.5`), `text` (enum `equal` \| `contains` \| `ignore`, whitespace normalized), `fonts_embedded` (bool) | — |
| `diagnostics` | `mode` (enum `exact` \| `contains` \| `absent`) | — |
| `scorecard` | `drop` (allowed drop per class, default `0`; floors only move up) | — |

`tolerance` may name a preset (`tolerance: render`) or give fields. A looser tolerance on an existing case is an expected-result change (see Expected results are protected).

### Size limits

| File | Limit |
|---|---|
| Each file in `input/` | 512 KB |
| Each PNG in `expected/` | 50 KB |
| One case directory in total | 1 MB |
| A kit's `cases/` in total | 50 MB |

Larger files belong to the corpus.

### The 10-minute budget

- Golden inputs are small: a few pages, a few hundred cells, images under 512 × 512, timelines under 3 seconds at 320 × 180. Large files belong to the corpus.
- Golden cases run in-process by default; the headless executable is exercised by the conformance suite and a few `golden` cases tagged `headless`.
- At most about ten `flow` cases per kit are `golden`; the rest are `corpus` (weekly).
- No `golden` case measures performance against a tight time budget on this shared machine; performance budgets (Q9) use generous limits in `golden` and the real numbers in the weekly report.
- Film exports in `golden` are a few frames, not a full export (the probe's 30-second 1080p export took 286 s).

## The feature catalogue: `features.yaml`

`features.yaml` is the only source; `FEATURES.md` is generated from it and never edited by
hand.

Top level:

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | int, `1` | yes | Version of this format |
| `kit` | string | yes | Canonical kit name (`doc`, `sheet`, `photo`, …) |
| `updated` | string, `YYYY-MM-DD` | yes | Last edit |
| `golden_budget_s` | int | yes | Wall-clock cap for all `golden` cases of the kit on the owner's machine; default and maximum `600` |
| `sources` | map<string, string> | no | Files the catalogue was generated from (`commands: crates/engine/engine/src/catalog.rs`, `parity: web/parity/photo-status.json`) |
| `protected` | list<string> | no | Extra globs treated like `cases/**/expected/` (see Expected results are protected): committed goldens and floors that live next to existing tests |
| `features` | list<feature> | yes | The catalogue |

Each feature:

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Feature id (see Names) |
| `title` | string | yes | Short English title |
| `direction` | list<enum> | yes | `function`, `conversion`, `ai`, `collab`, `fidelity` (the five directions), and for tests outside those five: `compat` (saved files open in the target application), `performance`, `robustness`, `data-safety`, `platform`, `security` |
| `priority` | enum `P0` \| `P1` \| `P2` | yes | P0 = must have for the kit's launch tier |
| `status` | enum `has` \| `partial` \| `missing` | yes | `has` = works end to end in the editor and survives save and reopen |
| `commands` | list<string> | no | Engine command ids the feature uses |
| `paths` | list<string> | no | Code globs; a change there selects this feature's cases (`--affected`) |
| `requirements` | list<string> | no | `kit-requirements.yaml` row ids |
| `parity` | list<string> | no | Keys in the kit's parity files |
| `target` | string | no | Reference application and version for this feature (`Word 16.113.4 (Mac)`) |
| `gap` | string | no | One sentence: the difference from the target application |
| `cases` | list<string> | generated | Case ids whose `feature` is this id. Written by `cargo xtask features`; the check fails when it differs from `cases/` |
| `corpus_files` | int | generated | Files in the corpus that exercise the feature (weekly run) |
| `since` | string, `YYYY-MM-DD` | yes | Date added |

Rules: a `P0` feature with `status: has` needs 1–3 `golden` cases (requirement Q2); a `missing` feature has none; a `partial` one has cases for what works.

## Expected results are protected

- Only the owner approves changes to expected results. "Expected results" are:
  1. every file under `cases/**/expected/` (added, changed, deleted or renamed);
  2. every path matched by `protected` in `features.yaml` (committed goldens and floors next to existing tests);
  3. in an existing `case.yaml`: any change to `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`, `input`, or `steps`, a move from `golden` to another layer, and deleting or moving the case directory;
  4. in `features.yaml`: removing a feature that has cases, or lowering its priority.
- Never change an expected result to make a test pass. If you believe one is wrong, stop and explain why in the task's findings.
- `external` references (made by a target application or an independent reader) are never regenerated by a tool. Only `self` references may be blessed, with `cargo xtask golden --bless <case-id>`, and only in a commit whose message has one line per case: `Expected-Change: <case-id>: <reason>`.
- New cases are listed too: the owner (or, if the owner decides, the second AI reviewer) checks that each new expected result comes from the reference the case names.
- A bug fix starts with the failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`: the pull request shows the case failing before the fix and passing after it.

kition-sdk's `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists, for a range of commits, every added, changed or
deleted expected result and every weakened test (deleted assertions or tests, added
`#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`). The review executor runs it on every candidate;
anything it lists goes to the owner and is never merged automatically.
